publication: Public summary of synthetic test validation. Full logs and workstation metadata remain local; no user habit data, credentials, local paths, process IDs or device identifiers are included.

designClauses.I97: docs/交互设计.md:97 requires write/read/delete testing before activation.
designClauses.D86: docs/数据与同步规范.md:86 requires a distinct certificate failure message.

scope.behavior: Configuration activation first verifies a fresh random probe in this device namespace, then creates and reads back the first encrypted business backup, then saves configuration.
scope.probe: 32 Random.secure bytes and a fresh UUID in access-<UUID>.probe; PUT If-None-Match:*; GET exact byte+SHA-256 match and valid strong ETag; DELETE If-Match; GET must be 404.
scope.tls: Typed dart:io TlsException (including HandshakeException) from send or response stream becomes a fixed redacted certificate/security-connection DavFailure. SocketException and generic http.ClientException have separate redacted connection messages.

targeted.skipReason: The explicitly provisioned real TLS WebDAV endpoint is not configured in this host invocation.

coveredScenarios: Success accepts DELETE 200 or 204 only after matching random bytes and strong ETag, confirms absence, and leaves pre-existing backup/user bytes unchanged.
Repeated access verification uses different filenames and random payloads, with no successful probe left behind.
PUT412/403, GET404, wrong bytes, missing/weak/malformed ETag, DELETE403/412, DELETE200 with residual file, timeout, and lost PUT response all reject capability validation.
No DELETE is attempted for an ambiguous collision, mismatched read, missing/weak/malformed ETag, or incomplete read; If-Match failure preserves another writer replacement.

Both new and previously configured UI: delete-permission failure saves no active configuration or first business backup, preserves all five draft fields and existing credentials/pointer, and leaves controller/repository facts unchanged.
The real controller plus MockHTTP UI test also triggers back and the old save callback before the first new frame, verifying the existing live busy guard permits one operation.

Repairing server permissions permits deliberate retry; only the new successful probe is deleted, the earlier inert failed probe and old/user files remain, the first real encrypted backup fully restores, and only then is the new pointer saved.
HandshakeException from both client send and response stream produces the dedicated redacted certificate message; a generic ClientException mentioning certificate text is not guessed to be TLS.

counterfactual.variant: Final UI with only verifyAccess call omitted; baseline upload/restore/save flow retained with current optional clientFactory seam.
counterfactual.baselineSaveBodyChecked: Baseline _save and variant _save match after substituting the optional current test client factory for the baseline constructor and normalizing whitespace.
counterfactual.failure: Omitting access verification reproduces the old flow: despite DELETE403, the active configuration ID changes from the expected existing ID to a new random ID.

realTlsTestChange.executionStatus: Updated and compiled by this target; actual real-service execution remains pending.
realTlsTestChange.conditionalNegative: When TEST_DAV_CERT is supplied for an integration-only CA absent from normal trust, a default SecurityContext IOClient must produce the redacted certificate failure and leave the random device directory empty.
realTlsTestChange.positive: The explicitly trusted client must complete verifyAccess with no probe left, followed by the existing real encrypted upload/list/restore/protected-import assertions.
realTlsTestChange.boundary: The untrusted-CA negative is conditional on explicit test CA configuration; public-certificate endpoints without TEST_DAV_CERT use the positive path.
realTlsTestChange.tlsPolicy: No badCertificateCallback, certificate-validation bypass, pinning, or global trust-store change was introduced.

limitations: New UI/server failure matrices use MockHTTP, real HabitController/MemoryHabitRepository, and native backup cryptography; they add no new Android/device or live-service result.
A successful retry removes its own verified probe; prior failed probes are retained for explicit manual cleanup because their current contents/version may be ambiguous.

Old-pointer protection here applies to probe/network/pre-store validation failures. Existing BackupSettingsStore commit/cleanup semantics are unchanged: _save commits the active pointer before status persistence, so later status/cleanup errors are not claimed to roll back a committed configuration.
